summary: @or-sdk/password preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundle on install
details: The package declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`. `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscator.io-style mangled (renamed identifiers, per-scope string tables hiding literals such as `ldd --version`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `bun`, `bun.exe`, `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, and the Bun release URL). At install time it downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/<arch>.zip` into a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], { stdio: 'inherit', cwd: D })`. The executed sibling `math_init.js` is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle at the tarball root with a shuffled string array, rotated integer table, and heavy identifier mangling; its filename is unrelated to the advertised password-reset SDK purpose. Executing the payload under Bun (rather than Node) means the actual install-time code is never parsed by Node-based tooling that follows require/import edges. A password SDK has no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime at install and use it to run an opaque bundled payload, and the combination of a mangled loader plus an obfuscated alternate-runtime payload matches the alternate-runtime dropper pattern used to evade install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
